---
title: "Getting started"
description: "Download the app and convert your first PDF."
---

There's nothing to build and nothing else to install. Download the app, open it, and convert. It takes about two minutes.

::: {.callout-note}
## What you need
- A Mac with Apple Silicon (an M1, M2, M3 or later chip). To check, open the Apple menu → **About This Mac** and look at **Chip**.
- A PDF that contains real text. A quick test: open the PDF and try to select a sentence with the mouse. If you can, it contains text. If the page behaves like one big picture, it's a scan, and the app can't read it (see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd#scanned-pdfs)).
:::

## Step 1: Download and install the app

1. Go to the [**Releases page**](https://github.com/pbeens/Petes-PDF-to-MD/releases). The newest release is at the top.
2. Under **Assets**, click **`Pete-s-PDF-to-MD-v1.0-macOS.dmg`** to download it. A DMG is a disk image, the usual way Mac apps are delivered.
3. Open the downloaded DMG and drag **Pete's PDF to MD** into your **Applications** folder.

[Go to the Releases page](https://github.com/pbeens/Petes-PDF-to-MD/releases){.btn .btn-primary role="button"}

::: {.callout-important}
## "Apple could not verify…" the first time you open it
The app isn't registered with Apple, so macOS blocks it the first time. To allow it:

1. Click **Done** (or **OK**) in the warning.
2. Open **System Settings → Privacy & Security** and scroll down.
3. Next to the message about Pete's PDF to MD, click **Open Anyway**, and confirm.

You only need to do this once.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Upgrading from version 0.8 or earlier?
Earlier versions needed Python and the PyMuPDF and pdf-inspector add-ons. Version 1.0 doesn't need them: everything it needs is built in. If you installed Python only for this app, you can leave it or remove it; the app no longer looks for it.
:::

## Step 2: Convert your first PDF

1. Open **Pete's PDF to MD** from your Applications folder.
2. Click **Select PDF** and choose a file, or drag a PDF from Finder and drop it anywhere on the window.
3. Next to **Output**, choose how you want the result split (you can change this later):
   - **One file**: the whole document in a single Markdown file.
   - **By major heading**: one file per top-level part or chapter.
   - **Individual sections**: one file per heading. This is the default.
4. Click **Run Conversion**. Most documents take a second or two.
5. When it finishes, the **Sections** list fills in. Click a section to read it, and tick **Render Markdown** to see it formatted instead of as plain text.
6. Click **Open Output Folder** to see the files in Finder.

By default the files go into **Documents → Pete's PDF to MD Output**, in a folder named after your PDF. Click **Change** next to *Output Root* to pick another place.

::: {.callout-note}
## If a warning appears
When something limits the conversion, a dialog tells you when it finishes. The most common one says that many pages are pictures with no text, which means the PDF is a scan; see [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd#scanned-pdfs).
:::

## Updating to a new version

Download the new DMG from the Releases page and drag the app into Applications again, replacing the old one.
